slides.heading: Task Assignment
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Greedy Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Task Assignment, a medium greedy algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: 2k tasks with durations, k workers doing two tasks each in parallel; minimise the longest worker time.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. 2k tasks with durations, k workers doing two tasks each in parallel; minimise the longest worker time. Pair shortest with longest. Returns index pairs.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Pair the shortest task with the longest so no worker gets two long tasks.
slides.narration: Pair the shortest task with the longest so no worker gets two long tasks.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: try every pairing → (2k)! / (2^k · k!)
Greedy: sort, pair ends → O(n log n)
slides.narration: Trying every pairing explodes combinatorially. Sorting and pairing the shortest with the longest balances the load in n log n. An exchange argument shows any other pairing can't lower the maximum.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort task indices by duration. Second, pair the ends moving inward. Third, return the index pairs.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Sort task indices by duration
slides.narration: Sort the task indices by duration, keeping the original indices so we can report them.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Pair shortest with longest: 1 + 5
slides.narration: Worker 1 gets the shortest remaining task, 1, with the longest, 5, for a total of 6.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Pair shortest with longest: 1 + 4
slides.narration: Worker 2 gets the shortest remaining task, 1, with the longest, 4, for a total of 5.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Pair shortest with longest: 3 + 3
slides.narration: Worker 3 gets the shortest remaining task, 3, with the longest, 3, for a total of 6.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We build a list of indices, sort it by task duration, and for i from zero to k pair the i-th smallest with the i-th largest.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Keep original indices (sort indices, not values)
slides.narration: Sort indices rather than values, so duplicates still map to the right task numbers.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: workers take more than two tasks (harder, partition-like)
slides.narration: Sketch the exchange argument briefly. If each worker can take more than two tasks, it becomes a much harder partition problem.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Pair the shortest task with the longest so no worker gets two long tasks.
slides.narration: To recap Task Assignment: Pair the shortest task with the longest so no worker gets two long tasks. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
